notes:
Compatibility: breaking for scripts

AI-DLC 2.11.5 rolls up the user-visible changes merged since 2.11.4: an answer to the plan question, whether its own choice, a plan's name or "go ahead" in your own words, from any chat, starts the request it asked about with the settings you typed with it; an approval is taken once, also when you ask for a fix and to go on in one reply, and one question for several stages shows every stage's open findings before you answer; `aidlc config` run by an older AI-DLC no longer takes down a project a newer one set up, and work a newer AI-DLC set up offers the update instead of a dead end; the first setup in a git repository says which files to commit for the team; a team Unit that conflicts with main is stopped before the merge question, not after your approval; Units Generation reads the mockups, and its checks name a story no Unit exposes; the developer builds from the whole code plan you approved; after a `git pull`, a teammate's files are no longer read as the build's change; the commands AI-DLC prints run as printed on a copy install, on Codex CLI and on Windows; HTML pages in the knowledge base are read as their text; Claude Code asks you to allow fewer commands you cannot judge; and corrections on every harness, Windows included.

Scripts are affected if they: run `aidlc config` in a project set up with a newer AI-DLC than the computer has; run `aidlc unit pin` on a Unit whose code conflicts with main; pass `--help`, or a flag or word the command does not take, to `aidlc system workspace-sync`, or a stray word to an `aidlc engine worktree` command; check the exit code of plugin sync in a project with no plugin installed; or read the `status` or the warning count of `aidlc doctor --json` and `--quiet`, or the `--quiet` lines of `aidlc config models` on Kiro. See Script compatibility below. Authors of plugins that bring their own agents for Kiro have one step below.

**Plugins:** a plugin that brings its own agents for Kiro gives them this release's shorter start (see Kiro under Harness by harness) once it is built again with `aidlc plugin build kiro` and installed again.

### Your words and your answers

* The plan question starts the request it asked about, however you answer it. On Claude Code, a plan's name typed alone as the reply (`bugfix`, also from a new chat) starts that request on that plan, instead of "What should I work on?" for a request already on record. On every harness, a reply in your own words (`/aidlc go ahead`, or "go ahead" in a new chat) starts the work with the depth, review level and Guard Policy you typed with the request, where it started at the plan's own with nothing said; and a review level typed with a request (`/aidlc --depth minimal --review none Fix the login crash when the session expires`) reaches the work whichever answer you pick.
* A setting typed among your words (`/aidlc express: add a --review advisory option`) applies however the agent passes your request on; on GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Kiro and opencode the review setting could be dropped, and a `--skip` or `--project-type` typed that way reaches new work too.
* With work in progress and the plan question for a separate request still waiting, a plan's name typed alone (`express`, in a new chat) no longer switches the work in progress to that plan, with its checks changed, while the request you were answering never started: the waiting request starts on that plan, or the agent asks you once which you meant. Asking in words to switch the work in progress ("switch the greeter work to the express plan") still switches it with no question.
* A plan question you left behind, by wording the request again or by starting another one, no longer counts as still waiting once the newer request has started work: a plan's name typed in a new chat starts your latest request, instead of bringing the approval question of the work in hand or "What should I work on?", and a reply in a new chat or your next request is no longer handed the dropped request's plan question.
* The question about where your words belong no longer offers work that is finished or archived, and does not come back once your words went on as a new request (in the same chat, in a new chat, or after `/clear`).
* Under a Guard Policy your team locked at strict, a request typed with a lower setting (`/aidlc --guard-policy relaxed <request>`, or `--plan-approval off`) starts at the team's strict with the other settings you typed, and the first step says once where the team set it and that changing that line changes it; before, nothing started on any of the plan question's answers.
* A choice the agent records as left to it now needs a reply of yours since that question was asked, so the record no longer says you answered a question you were never shown (on opencode, an Approve at Reverse Engineering could run on into Requirements Analysis and record "Guide me" and a requirements answer in your name). "Up to you" after the question, or "pick the defaults" in your first request, still counts and is not asked again.
* On Claude Code, Codex CLI and Kiro (Kiro IDE, and Kiro CLI on its v3 engine), AI-DLC reads your request from the line you typed, not from the agent's retyping of it, on Claude Code's shortcuts too (`/aidlc-bugfix`, `/aidlc-compose`, `/aidlc-init` and the others); on Claude Code and Codex CLI the plan question quotes it as you typed it.

### Gates, reviews, and plan approval

* An approval is taken once. "Fix R-01 and R-02 as suggested, then go on" at a reviewed gate approves it after the agent makes the fix, instead of the gate being shown again for a second approval; under Guard Policy strict, an approval you give after the changed document was reviewed goes through (after a change you asked for mid-stage was revised and reviewed, or, with the review freeze off, after a recovery review brought a new finding), where the record gained a Request Changes you did not give and you were asked again; and an Approve at a team Unit's gate is no longer stopped with `report --result approved for unit ... requires --user-input with the human's reply.` and asked again.
* One question for several stages (Construction Unit by Unit, with Unit checkpoints off) shows every listed stage's open findings before you answer, where it showed the first stage's and said none were open; "Approve, and fix the rate limit point in NFR Requirements" approves every listed stage and records that fix with its stage, instead of refusing the whole approval; and a stage whose review is recorded after your answer and raises a finding shows its own gate first, instead of being approved with the finding recorded as a risk you accepted and never saw.
* The code plan question: in work with several repositories it names the repositories the plan names files in, in one line that is never cut (`Names files in api and web.`); an answer you write after `[Answer]:` in `code-generation-questions.md` stays when AI-DLC writes the file again (after you save a source file, a resume or a new chat, or on a copy with Windows line endings), instead of coming back blank; and an approved plan stays approved when a Testing Posture section of `org.md`, `team.md` or `project.md` gains a blank line, trailing spaces or a comment, where under strict the next write was refused and the same plan asked again.
* While a code plan waits for your approval, a read command that starts another program or writes a file through an option (`rg --pre <program>`, `sort --compress-program <program>`, `git grep -O<program>`, `sort --o=<file>`) waits for the plan, like any command AI-DLC cannot read; a plain read, and a program run directly, are as before.
* A stage's gate is no longer refused over a tool cache your `.gitignore` keeps out of git (`.hypothesis/`, a test run's reports) once every Unit is reviewed, where the one recovery review was spent on the same list and the only way on was to redo the stage; an edit to a file git tracks is still named and still refuses.
* The lint check reports a file's lint errors however many there are, instead of `The linter check could not run on <file>.` once ESLint's result passed about 1 MiB (a file with about 4,000 errors).
* On Claude Code you are asked less often to allow a command you cannot judge at a gate or a review: a gate that opens with a check still failing tells the agent which file holds the findings, so it no longer searches for it with a shell line; and the reviewer is told its review folder already exists, so its own `mkdir -p` came up in 2 of 24 measured runs instead of 7 of 16.

### Mockups, Units Generation, and traceability

* Refined Mockups runs for a project with a user interface on the classic and workshop plans, designed from the user stories and requirements; before, its condition asked for rough mockups from Ideation, which those plans do not run, so the agent could report the stage as skipped.
* Units Generation reads the refined mockups when there are any, and its review reports a story no Unit exposes, or a mockup screen no Unit builds, as a Major finding, instead of saying the plan is ready while a story's screen has no Unit.
* The traceability check at Units Generation: a story whose row names only `library`, `spec` or `packaging` Units is named until the row adds the `ui` or `service` Unit that exposes it or says how it is reached in a column headed `Reached through` (`existing: <where>` or `interface`); when the Unit plan is made again after Units finished, a story whose Units are all finished and never built one of its criteria is named, with the step to add a Unit that is not finished; and a story your team keeps out of every Unit (handled in Operation, say) settles with `none` in its Units cell and a `Deferred` row giving the reason, also at Build and Test.
* A criterion one Unit hands to another (an `N/A` row whose target is that Unit) counts as built only when that Unit builds it: the Unit's own check names a hand-off to a Unit that is not on the story's row, and Build and Test lists a criterion no Unit built as uncovered, where it read as covered.
* Work under way is asked nothing about these changes: a Refined Mockups or Units Generation that already finished stands as it is, the work's record notes once that AI-DLC now does the stage differently, and `/aidlc --stage refined-mockups` runs a Refined Mockups that was skipped.

### Construction

* The developer builds from the whole code plan you approved. On Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and opencode, AI-DLC hands the developer the plan and its test instructions as it starts, instead of whatever the agent retyped into its start message; on the other harnesses the agent is given the exact command whose output it passes on. In measured Claude Code runs the developer read both files whole before its first write in 6 of 6, where no start had carried them whole, and its own shell lines on the plan asked you 2 times instead of 8.
* Working alone, a Unit's checkpoint lists the open findings of the Unit's earlier stages (Functional Design, NFR Requirements, NFR Design, Infrastructure Design) ahead of Code Generation's review, and Approve records exactly the findings it showed; before, it said no findings were open and the record said you had accepted them.
* "Approve it as it is" at a Unit's checkpoint approves a Unit whose check did not pass (every test green under a coverage threshold, say) in one step, recorded with your words and the failed run, and you hear "Approved. core's check, `bun test --coverage test/`, did not pass."; before, the approval was refused and the same check ran again. Under a strict Guard Policy your team locked the check stays required, said once with where it is set; a check that timed out, was interrupted or could not run is not gone over.
* A change you ask for to one Unit is made: Request Changes, or a change, for the Unit on a step that is written and reviewed reopens that step for that Unit, with its revised plan back for your approval, instead of a refusal or an order to record its completion first; and a change asked of a Unit paused at its step is made ("Making your change in Code Generation for unit beta.") instead of the pause question again. Every other Unit keeps its files, reviews and approvals.
* After a plain `git pull` during Code Generation, the files a teammate's commit brought are no longer read as the build's change: the build's approval no longer names them with a `git checkout` line that would undo the teammate's commit in your folder, the code plan question no longer lists them under "Already changed before you approved", and with Units under Guard Policy strict the close of Code Generation is no longer refused over them. A file the build itself changed is still named, and its way back puts back the teammate's copy; a change the build made is left out the same way once it is pushed and merged here, and one that is only on this machine is named as before.
* Code kept in a repository beside the project and recorded for the work (`/aidlc intent add-checkout ../shop-web`): under Guard Policy strict or relaxed the Unit's review reads, searches and tests it by its path from the project, instead of each read being refused with `This review cannot open "../shop-web/app.js" because it belongs to another unit`; and a traceability row that points at a file there is followed to the file, instead of the gate reporting `target escapes the project directory` for files that exist and Build and Test reading those requirements as not built.
* Each Unit's test command is recorded so it runs as written from the project root, with any folder it needs inside the command, so the Unit's review and Build and Test run the same command instead of each working one out from a note such as "run these from web/".
* `aidlc engine worktree purge` and `restore` refuse a word they do not read, such as a stamp or a day count typed without its flag name (`purge --slug payments 30`), where purge deleted every parked attempt for that slug, the only copies kept, and restore checked out the newest; `list` and `info` refuse one too.

### Team work and Units

* `/aidlc unit pin` tries the Unit's merge with main before the merge question. A Unit whose code conflicts with one that landed since it published is refused there, with the files and the owner's next step (`Unit "alpha" source conflicts: src/shared.ts. Nothing was pinned.`, then where to merge main, resolve and publish again), and "push main first" when main here holds a landing not pushed yet; before, the conflict showed only at land, after you had approved the merge.
* The team board says where the Units stand in plain words: which Units are claimed and by whom, when this checkout last saw a team's branch move, which merges wait and what is next for each, and whether the main checkout can go on.
* Pin takes a Unit whose stages main had sent back before the claim and the clone sent back once more, instead of `Pinned candidate evidence is incomplete: UNIT_COMPLETED receipts.`; and a step you skipped on main for every Unit before any claim stays skipped for the Unit a team then claims, with your reason at the merge question, instead of being handed to the team again and refused at pin.
* On a team's main: a redo of Units Generation keeps every landed Unit's work, so the Units that wait on it can be claimed and the landed skeleton is not offered again; after main moves on to Build and Test while teams hold Units, switching to building the Units alone, or changing when their approvals are asked, stays refused with the lines you meet before the move; and a redo that is not done for every Unit says why once ("Functional Design is not redone for every unit once a team has taken a unit: ...") with no `/aidlc --doctor` line or error box after it.
* In a team Unit: the recovery choice that records one stage as done reads "Mark Functional Design done" instead of "Mark this Unit finished"; and under the end-of-Unit rhythm a step whose documents the agent wrote before starting it is started at its first record, instead of the later stages being built on it and you being asked about it at the Unit's end.
* A claim whose file is kept in the project's `aidlc/` folder (`aidlc/.aidlc-unit-claim.json`), as a teammate on a later AI-DLC may write it, is read by status, claim, publish, pin, the merge question, land and release, instead of each stopping with `Unit claim registry fetch failed: ...`; and a landing leaves claim files and a Unit's result folder off main.

### Knowledge base and team documents

* An HTML page (a spec exported from Word, Confluence or Google Docs) added with `/aidlc knowledge onboard` is stored as its text, with tables as Markdown tables, in the page's own encoding, instead of raw markup that filled the 200,000-character cap with tags, styles and inline images; a Windows-1252 page is read instead of `unsupported_type`. Pages added before are read at the next `/aidlc knowledge sync`; to keep a page's markup (a UI mockup), add a copy saved with a `.txt` name.
* On Claude Code and GitHub Copilot, the first chat in a teammate's clone has the team's and the project's own rules (`team.md` and `project.md`: a saved conversation language, a scope override) before its first step, so a bare `/aidlc` no longer opens in English for a team that saved another language; and that chat is no longer sent to read AI-DLC's seven method files first, which on Claude Code could ask you to allow a shell loop nobody asked for.

### Setup, configuration, and lifecycle

* `aidlc version` reports `2.11.5` on all seven harnesses.
* `aidlc config` no longer takes a project down to an older release. In a project set up with a newer AI-DLC than this computer has, nothing changes and one line names both ways on (`Nothing changed: this project was set up with AI-DLC <its release>, and this computer is on <yours>. To carry on: ...`): the update to the project's release, or the pin that takes the project down on purpose. At a terminal on a native install config asks once whether to update this computer and then carries on with the same command. Before, `aidlc config --yes`, the step `aidlc update` names, rewrote the project's files to the older release, removed the files it did not know and said "Updated."
* Work whose record a newer AI-DLC wrote offers the update instead of a refusal in engine words. On a native install you are asked once ("This plan was set up with a newer AI-DLC, and this computer has 2.11.5. Want me to update AI-DLC now and carry on?"), and a yes updates AI-DLC, refreshes the project and carries on with what you typed. A copied install, a pinned project, a package manager's install and an unattended run get one line with their own step; doctor, `aidlc unit claim` and `aidlc unit release` say the same, and no Unit of such work is claimed from the older release.
* The first `aidlc config` for a harness in a git repository says once which files git does not track yet (`Note: git does not track AI-DLC's setup for Claude Code in this project yet: .claude/, aidlc/ and .gitignore. Commit them so teammates who use Claude Code get the same setup.`), and `aidlc doctor` shows that line for as long as it holds, where it named only `git add aidlc/`. Nothing is staged or committed for you.
* A command AI-DLC prints runs as printed. On a copy install, config's steps, refusals and `--show` list, the diagnostics' fixes, usage lines and the team board's merge steps name the install's own command (`bun <harness folder>/tools/aidlc.ts ...`), with `--harness` when the project has two harnesses and `--project-dir` when run from another folder; Codex CLI's runner skills say `$aidlc`; a folder name with a space is quoted; refusals the agent meets name commands that exist instead of tool files; `aidlc system rollback <version>` for a version this machine does not hold says it is not installed; and a mistyped `/aidlc plugin` or `/aidlc knowledge` verb names the commands that exist. On a Claude Code copy install you now meet the Allow prompt for a Unit claim, as on a native install.
* `aidlc doctor` and `aidlc config` run with `--project-dir` from another folder say `Project folder for this report: <path> (not the folder you ran doctor from).` above their fixes, so a fix copied as printed is not run on the wrong project; and `config <section> --check` gives its next step with `--project-dir`, and with `--harness` in a project with more than one harness.
* `aidlc system workspace-sync --help` (or `-h`, or `help`) prints its usage and changes nothing, and a flag or word it does not take (`--dry-run`, a mistyped `--forse`, `status`) is refused by name (`workspace-sync does not take --forse; nothing was changed`), where each ran a real sync: repositories cloned, the managed `.gitignore` block rewritten and `aidlc.code-workspace` written. On a native install doctor's workspace rows name `aidlc system workspace-sync`, where they named a command that does not exist, and the guide says how to run the sync where the shell has no `aidlc` command.
* In a project pinned with `aidlc config --pin`, the pinned release is checked in full once per session instead of on every command and hook call, so each call after the session's first waits about half as long (measured 0.49 s to 0.23 s on Linux, 0.88 s to 0.53 s on Windows Server); `aidlc update`, `aidlc use`, `aidlc config --pin` and `aidlc doctor` still check in full. And `aidlc config` there writes the five scope runner skills from the pinned release, not the active one, so teammates on different releases no longer flip those files in each other's diffs.
* `aidlc doctor` no longer warns `Hook failures ... review-freeze ... "State file not found"` after a plugin selection or `knowledge onboard` in a project with no work yet; and the cost shown prices Claude Fable 5.2, Opus 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5 at their list rates, where their use was left out of the total.
* The guides: the Codex CLI manual copy saves a project's own `.codex/config.toml`, `hooks.json` and `rules/default.rules` in `.codex/before-aidlc/` before copying, and the Kiro page says to move a copied project to a newer release with its setup command alone, which keeps its plugin choices and setup answers.

### Plugins

* `/aidlc plugin sync` in a project with no plugin installed and nothing composed says `no installed plugins; nothing to sync`, instead of failing with `host inventory unavailable; run sync through an installed plugin's host hook`; plugin select and sync errors name the command you typed; `aidlc plugin validate` and `aidlc plugin build` show their own usage and name a flag they do not take; and the authoring guide's example doctor check names `/aidlc plugin sync` instead of a Bun command a native install has no Bun for.
* On opencode with a copied runtime, a plugin's own tool that plugin sync installed runs (`bun .aidlc/tools/<plugin-tool>.ts ...`), so a plugin stage that runs its tool can finish; a file no sync installed, or one changed since the sync, is refused in one plain line with the sync command that runs.

### Harness by harness

* Claude Code: a stage gate's own notices (that the project has no git, what Approve accepts with findings open) show in the question box under the agent's question, word for word, instead of in the agent's words beside it; with Claude Code's own sandbox on, on Linux, AI-DLC's commands know which chat they run in, so a second chat keeps its own work and a stage step no longer carries every rule again; and when a reviewer, a support agent or the Code Generation developer works in the background, the agent keeps waiting in the same turn and goes on when that helper returns, instead of ending its turn or waiting on files that are written only afterwards.
* Codex CLI: a turn that started a helper (a scan, a review) and ended without waiting for it is carried on with "AI-DLC is carrying on with <stage>.", instead of the work sitting until you type "continue"; setup's trust step names the question Codex CLI asks at start ("start Codex in the project folder and choose Trust all and continue when it asks about hooks") instead of a `/hooks` step with nothing left to trust; and a stage document written through an `apply_patch` heredoc is no longer refused as a write to AI-DLC's audit trail when its Markdown holds `> $5`, `retries > 3?` or `> **Note**`.
* GitHub Copilot: after a chat is compacted, the agent gets the workflow's place and rules back with its next tool result, once per compaction, instead of retrying wrong flags and repeating a review pass for the rest of the chat.
* Kiro: at a terminal with Kiro CLI 2.24.1 or later found, Enter at `aidlc config`'s harness question sets up Kiro (Kiro IDE, and Kiro CLI on its v3 engine) where it took Kiro CLI (V2); type 5, or run `aidlc config --harness kiro-v2`, for Kiro CLI (V2), and `--yes`, `--harness` and a project already set up pick what they picked before. `aidlc config models`, its `--check` and doctor name an agent model that is not in Kiro CLI's model list, since Kiro runs such an agent on your chat's model without saying so. Each helper starts with five shared knowledge files (about 18,000 characters) instead of the aidlc agent's whole skill (about 94,000). And in a Kiro CLI chat driven through an ACP client, where AI-DLC's hooks do not run, the agent is told a save cannot be recorded there and how to get back, instead of saving the same document again every turn. An Always allow rule you narrowed by hand to exactly AI-DLC's bare first command no longer covers that command, so Kiro asks for it again; the rule Kiro itself offers (`bun *`) covers it.
* opencode: every helper starts with what AI-DLC hands it (the developer with the whole approved plan, as above); and the first-setup note names the `opencode.jsonc` a team keeps.
* Windows: a command or hook waiting on a lock carries on when the lock is let go just as it is read, instead of `<folder>\.aidlc-transaction.lock cannot be read.` with a step to delete a folder that was already gone; a refusal to read a hard-linked file says the way past it in words every shell reads ("Copy the file, delete the original, give the copy the original's name, then re-run."), not a `cp ... && mv ...` line; doctor's commit step reads `git add aidlc/`, `git commit`, `git push` instead of a `&&` chain Windows PowerShell 5.1 cannot parse; the installer's messages name its parameters as PowerShell takes them; and a path with an apostrophe in a user folder's name is quoted so Git Bash reads it too.

### Script compatibility

* Breaking for scripts: in a project set up with a newer AI-DLC than this computer has, `aidlc config` changes nothing and exits 5 with the step to take (`{ "ok": true, "status": "action-needed" }` under `--json`), where it rewrote the project's files to the older release and exited 0. That holds with `--yes`, `--harness`, `--force`, `--mcp` and `--dry-run`, and for a section that refreshes (such as `config project`). Update the computer first (`aidlc update --version <the project's release>`) or pin the project. `--pin`, `--unpin`, `--from`, a pinned project, the copy channel and the sections that write only records (`models`, `flags`, `runtime`, `providers`, `trust`) are unchanged.
* Breaking for scripts: `aidlc unit pin` exits 1 with `Unit "<unit>" source conflicts: <files>. Nothing was pinned.` for a Unit whose merge with main would conflict, where it pinned the Unit and `aidlc unit land` refused it; with a git older than 2.38 the check stays with land.
* Breaking for scripts: `aidlc system workspace-sync` prints its usage, exits 0 and changes nothing for `--help`, `-h` or `help`, and exits 1 with `workspace-sync does not take <flag>; nothing was changed` for a flag or word it does not take (such as `--dry-run` or `status`), where before each ran the sync. A bare sync, `--force`, `--project-dir <path>`, and `--json`, `--quiet`, `--no-color`, `--yes` and `--verbose` run as before.
* Breaking for scripts: `aidlc engine worktree purge`, `restore`, `list` and `info` exit 1 with `worktree <verb> does not take "<word>". Valid flags: ...` for a word that is not a flag's value, where the word was passed over and the command ran (a `purge` then deleted every parked attempt for the slug).
* Breaking for scripts: `aidlc engine plugin sync` in a Claude Code or Codex CLI project with no plugin installed and nothing composed exits 0 with `no installed plugins; nothing to sync`, where it exited 1 with `host inventory unavailable; ...`.
* Breaking for scripts: `aidlc doctor --json` and `--quiet` count one more warning per harness whose setup files git does not track yet, and on Kiro one per agent model that is not in Kiro CLI's model list, so `"status"` can read `"warning"` where it read `"ok"`; `ok` and the exit code are unchanged. On Kiro, `aidlc config models --quiet` prints such a model as a `Warning:` line and `--json` adds `agentModels`.
